ideas.ablation_behavior_off: eta_i := 0 for all i (and s_i unused), so the assignment metric is the exact Poincare distance at the same curvature; the run must be identical in code path except that the behaviour terms are zero. Not trained this round, only present and correct in the config.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the single trained run: C derived from the train median feature norm and eta_i from the train successor table, both active in every level's assignment.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: C := 0, so exp_0 and log_v collapse to identity and the distance is the plain Euclidean squared distance with sqrt(1 - eta cos^2) still active, i.e. a behaviour-anisotropic Mahalanobis-level RQ; the code path is shared, only the curvature branch changes. Not trained this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: From TRAIN-split user sessions only. For every ordered pair (i,j) occurring in the same training session with j in positions t+1..t+3 after i, increment count(i->j); drop edges with count < 2; row-normalise to p_ij over the 24556 training item ids; eta_i = max_j p_ij clipped to [0,0.9]; s_i = sum_j p_ij f_j with f the frozen input feature table of the same 24556 items. Computed once before Stage 2 and frozen.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item successor flow with its confidence: for each item, the normalised distribution over next items and the top-1 mass, plus the successor-weighted anchor vector.
ideas.cost_estimate:
Offline once: sparse 24556x24556 training transition matrix and 24556 successor anchors, minutes on CPU, memory ~nnz floats. Per step at the frozen scale (24556 items, 24 steps/epoch, batch ~1023, L=3 levels, K=256): the baseline makes ~786k squared

distances per step; SUCC-ANISO-RQ makes the same 786k but each costs one Mobius difference plus one artanh instead of a subtraction and a dot product, i.e. roughly 2.5x the assignment kernel; the per-item anchor log map is 1023 evaluations per step and is cacheable per epoch. Expect the quantizer block to cost ~2.5x and the whole step ~1.4-1.6x, i.e. total Stage 2 wall clock 1.4-1.6x baseline, with no extra parameters and no extra memory of note.
ideas.coupling_equation: k_l(i) = argmin_k (2/sqrt(C)) artanh( sqrt(C) * ||log_{v_l}^C(c_{l,k})|| * sqrt(1 - eta_i * <log_{v_l}^C(c_{l,k})/||.||, log_{v_l}^C(exp_0^C(s_i))/||.||>^2) ), with eta_i = w_behaviour(i) = top-1 training successor mass and the artanh/log terms being the curved part; v_l = exp_0^C(r_{l-1}).
ideas.coupling_path:
The training successor d

irection u_i and confidence eta_i of item i directly define the metric tensor at the current residual point, the metric tensor defines the curved distance to each level-l code, and that distance produces the level-l code index; the code index is the SID prefix. There is one path only: item -> (train transitions) -> (u_i, eta_i) -> deformed Poincare distance -> argmin_k at level l -> prefix token. Setting eta_i = 0 deletes the behaviour from the distance and restores the exact Poincare distance; setting C = 0 deletes the curvature and restores the exact Euclidean squared distance; neither switch can be removed without changing the produced SID.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the first SID token should encode next intent rather than surface content, then the coupled run must show (a) a materially different level-1 code histogram than the Euclidean run, with items that are content twins but behaviourally divergent split at level 1, (b) higher next-prefix predictability measured on train-split held-out-by-time transitions, and (c) Stage 3 test_recall@10 above 0.065. It is worth keeping if (a) happens together with (b); it is dropped if the level-1 partition is unchanged (deformation too weak relative to the residual scale) or if recall is at or below baseline.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ-VAE quantizer, at the nearest-code decision of every level l = 1..L of the prefix hierarchy (and therefore in the objective that shapes the codebook through the resulting assignments). It changes which code wins, hence which prefix every item receives at every depth.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature -C with sqrt(C) = artanh(0.5)/median_train||f||; Poincare ball exp/log maps, Mobius difference, and a rank-one anisotropic deformation of the Poincare metric, G_i(v) = lambda(v)^2 (I - eta_i u_i(v) u_i(v)^T) with lambda(v) = 2/(1 - C||v||^2), collapsed into the closed-form curved distance d~ = (2/sqrt(C)) artanh(sqrt(C) ||log_v^C(c)|| sqrt(1 - eta_i cos^2 theta)).
ideas.key_change: Each item i gets a fixed unit behaviour direction u_i and a behaviour confidence eta_i from its training successor distribution; the level-l code is chosen by nearest neighbour under a deformed Poincare distance that contracts lengths along u_i by a factor sqrt(1 - eta_i cos^2 theta), evaluated at the current residual point with fixed negative curvature C. Removing the behaviour sets eta = 0 (pure Poincare RQ); removing the curvature sets C = 0 (plain Euclidean RQ-VAE).
ideas.leakage_boundary: Only training-split sequences enter the transition counts, the anchors and eta; the item universe is exactly the 24556 training items; validation and test interactions are never read, no validation-derived statistic (no tuning, no early stopping) and no test-time prefix frequency is used; every constant (C, eta clip, window, count threshold) is derived from the train median feature norm, from the train transition table, or is a documented default fixed before the run.
ideas.motivation: In a plain RQ-VAE the level-1 token splits items by static content similarity, so the first SID token carries no information about where the user actually goes next; the generative model then has to spend capacity re-deriving intent from token 2 and 3. Items that are content-twins but have disjoint successor sets share a prefix (prefix collisions that matter behaviourally), and items with the same next-intent but different surface features get different prefixes. Both hurt next-item recall at short prefix depth.
ideas.novelty: The geometry is used to change the SHAPE of the per-level quantization cells, not their radius, their centroids or their curvature scalar. Previous mechanisms here moved codebook means (successor-weighted Frechet/Karcher), set a scalar curvature per level from prefix-transition score, or ranked codes radially by context entropy, or used entailment cones. Here the codebooks, the curvature per level and the Euclidean residual chain are left exactly as in the baseline; what changes is that each item carries its own rank-one deformation of the Poincare metric, aligned with the direction of its training successor flow, so the nearest-code decision at every level measures distance in a behaviour-elongated curved metric. Note explicitly that Mobius transport alone is an isometry and would be a no-op; this mechanism is deliberately non-isometric.
ideas.observables: (1) Fraction of items whose level-1 code changes relative to the Euclidean run, and the per-level code histograms; (2) mean hyperbolic prefix-path length and prefix-collision structure; (3) next-prefix predictability on train-split time-held-out transitions (given prefix_{1..l}, how often prefix_{l+1} matches the held-out successor's prefix); (4) Stage 3 test_recall@10, the only judgement.

rejected_ideas.reason: out of scope: ablation_geometry_off does not say what replaces the curve

risks: The deformation could be swamped at level 1 because the first residual is dominated by the item's own feature norm, so the angle term matters little; eta_i from a noisy top-1 successor could make cells unstable for low-count items (mitigated by count>=2 and eps-shrinkage); bending the metric per item can create asymmetric or intransitive neighbourhoods, so a minority of items may get codes that no other item shares, wasting vocabulary; the behaviour anchor built from raw features may be a poor proxy for the encoder's learned space late in training.
ideas.safeguards: clamp every artanh argument to [0, 1-1e-5]; eps = 1e-8 in all norms and normalisations; eta clipped to [0, 0.9] guarantees positive definiteness of I - eta u u^T; items with zero kept successors get eta=0 so they fall back to the exact Poincare (or Euclidean) distance rather than inventing a direction; s_i standardised to the feature scale of f before use so the anchor direction is not dominated by a single popular successor; sqrtC computed from the train median and frozen so the ball never collapses (median radius 0.5, max radius < 1); the C->0 branch implemented separately (tanh/artanh removed) instead of dividing by C; distance evaluation in float32 with the ||w|| = 0 case returning exactly 0.
ideas.spec_equations:
# offline
for (i,j,dt) in train_sessions: if 1 <= dt <= 3: cnt[i,j] += 1
cnt[cnt < 2] = 0;  p[i,:] = cnt[i,:] / max(sum_j cnt[i,j], eps)
eta[i] = clip(max_j p[i,j], 0, 0.9) if sum_j cnt[i,j] > 0 else 0
s[i]  = sum_j p[i,j] * f[j]                       # frozen feature table
sqrtC = artanh(0.5) / median_i ||f[i]||           # derived, per dataset
# per step, per item, per level
def exp0(x):  n = sqrtC*||x||;  return (tanh(n)/max(n,eps)) * x        # sqrtC=0 -> identity
def logv(v, c):
    a = -v
    num = (1 + 2C<a,c> + C||c||^2)*a + (1 - C||a||^2)*c
    den = 1 + 2C<a,c> + C^2||a||^2||c||^2
    t   = ||num/den||
    coef = (2/C) * artanh(clamp(sqrtC*t, 0, 1-1e-5)) / max(t,eps)   # limit 2t/... as C->0
    return coef * (num/den)
w = logv(v_l, exp0(E[l][k]));  g = logv(v_l, exp0(s[i]))
cos2 = (<w,g>/(||w||*||g||+eps))^2
d2 = ( (2/sqrtC) artanh(clamp(sqrtC*||w||*sqrt(1 - eta[i]*cos2), 0, 1-1e-5)) )^2
k_l = argmin_k d2 ;  r_l = r_{l-1} - E[l][k_l] ;  v_{l+1} = exp0(r_l)
# loss unchanged: RQ-VAE reconstruction on sum_l E[l][k_l]; gradient to E[l][k_l] via straight-through
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs:
Inputs: encoder output e_i in R^d per item in the batch, per-level codebooks E[l] in R^{K x d}, frozen per-item successor anchor s_i in R^d, frozen per-item confidence eta_i in [0,0.9], curvature constant C, number of levels L. Outputs: code index seq

uence (k_1..k_L) = the item's SID, the Euclidean residuals r_l, and the unchanged reconstruction x_hat; the straight-through gradient w.r.t. E[l] and the encoder.

specification.text: Fixed curvature C (derived, below). Ball map exp_0^C(x) = tanh(sqrt(C)||x||) x/(sqrt(C)||x||), C>0, identity when C=0. Mobius difference a (+) _C b = ((1 + 2C<a,b> + C||b||^2) a + (1 - C||a||^2) b) / (1 + 2C<a,b> + C^2 ||a||^2 ||b||^2), a = -v. Log map log_v^C(c) = (2/(sqrt(C)(1 - C||v||^2))) artanh(sqrt(C)||(-v)(+)_C c||) * ((-v)(+)_C c)/||(-v)(+)_C c||. Per item: successor weights p_ij = count_train(i->j)/sum_j count_train(i->j), top-1 mass eta_i = p_i,max clipped to [0, 0.9], successor anchor s_i = sum_j p_ij f_j (f = fixed input item feature, not the moving encoder output), u_i(v) = log_v^C(exp_0^C(s_i))/||log_v^C(exp_0^C(s_i))||. Deformed distance d~(v,c) = (2/sqrt(C)) artanh( sqrt(C) ||w|| sqrt(1 - eta_i <w/||w||, u_i(v)>^2) ), w = log_v^C(c). RQ loop becomes v_l = exp_0^C(r_{l-1}), c_{l,k} = exp_0^C(E_l[k]), k_l = argmin_k d~_i(v_l, c_{l,k}), r_l = r_{l-1} - E_l[k_l]; decoder and reconstruction loss unchanged. Derived constants: sqrt(C) = artanh(0.5)/median_train||f|| (so the median item sits at ball radius 0.5); transition window = same session, target within next 3 positions; edges with count < 2 dropped; if an item has no kept successor, eta_i = 0.

ideas.title: Successor-direction anisotropic Poincare metric inside every RQ-VAE level assignment (behaviour stretches the quantization cells, curvature bends them)

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: pi_p replaced by the uniform distribution over successor clusters and H(p) replaced by the residual-variance criterion (split the highest-residual-variance prefix of each level, same insertion budget, same curved radius, same geometry), so the growth still happens but is not behaviour-selected and has no behaviour direction (the direction falls back to the top principal tangent direction of the parent's residual cloud).
ideas.ablation_both_on: H(p) > log 2 selects the prefix, pi_p supplies b_p, and c_new = exp_{c_{l,k}}( arcsinh(2^{1/(n-1)} sinh rho_p) * u_p ) is inserted into level l+1; this is the arm that is trained (the only arm trained in this round).
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: identical behaviour path (same H(p), same b_p, same prefixes chosen) but the insertion is Euclidean: c_new = c_{l,k} + s_E * (b_p - c_{l,k})/||b_p - c_{l,k}|| with s_E = 2^{1/(n-1)} * rho_p on the uncurved coordinates, no exp/log, radius linear instead of sinh.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the TRAINING split only, before Stage 2: build sparse C[i,i'] = number of directed consecutive pairs (i followed by i' within a training session window) over the 24556 training items, symmetrised optional-free (directed kept as is). Frozen thereafter. At each growth pass, using the current item->prefix assignment (k_1..k_l) available from the epoch's own forward passes (cached, no extra pass): for each prefix p, S_p = items with that prefix, pi_p(j) = (sum_{i in S_p} sum_{i' in S_j} C[i,i']) / Z_p with Z_p the total outgoing mass of S_p, H(p) = -sum_j pi_p(j) log pi_p(j) in nats.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed training-item transitions aggregated to prefix level: the successor entropy H(p) of every level-l SID prefix p, together with the successor mass distribution pi_p over level-l prefix clusters that supplies the barycentre direction (behavioural branching / user-interest branching).
ideas.cost_estimate: Baseline 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72000 steps. Growth overhead: 12 passes x (one sparse aggregation over the frozen transition matrix, ~5e5 nonzeros, plus a 24556-item Einstein-midpoint reduction, plus a 24556 x L SID refresh) = O(12 * (5e5 + 7e4)) ops, a few milliseconds per pass, < 0.1% of wall clock. Per-step cost at the frozen scale (24556 items, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs) is unchanged except the level-l nearest-codeword matmul grows by at most the insertion count: entropy-gated growth adds <= ~12% codewords per level, i.e. <= ~12% on that microsecond-scale matmul, well under 1% of a step. No extra forward/backward pass is added.
ideas.coupling_equation: H(p) = -sum_j pi_p(j) log pi_p(j) > log 2  =>  c_new = exp_{c_{l,k}} ( s(rho_p) * u_p ), u_p = log_{c_{l,k}}(b_p)/||log_{c_{l,k}}(b_p)||_L, s(rho_p) = arcsinh( 2^{1/(n-1)} sinh rho_p ), b_p = EinsteinMidpoint( {e_{i'} : i' successor of S_p}, weights pi_p ), rho_p = median_{i in S_p} d_c(v_i, c_{l,k}).
ideas.coupling_path: behaviour entropy decides whether prefix p splits -> the same behaviour mass pi_p defines the barycentre b_p and therefore the tangent direction u_p at the parent codeword -> the curvature-derived radius s(rho_p) converts that direction into an actual point in the ball -> that point becomes a codeword of level l+1 -> which changes which residual each item is assigned to and hence every downstream SID prefix. Behaviour without geometry has no position; geometry without behaviour has no target prefix.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis:
Behaviourally branching prefixes are the ones that cap Stage 3 prefix predictability, and a co

deword placed at the curvature-correct distance from the parent is the right amount of new resolution there (too close = no separation, too far = hijacks other regions). If true, the conditional successor entropy of the sharpened prefixes drops after growth, the level-(l+1) usage mass of the new codewords is dominated by their parent prefix's items, and Stage 3 test_recall@10 moves above the 0.065 target in the single frozen run.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the quantization itself, as a discrete topological update of the RQ codebooks between Stage 2 epochs (a curved codeword-birth operator acting on the hierarchy levels 1..L-1), not as a loss.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare exp map at the parent codeword, exp_{c_p}: T_{c_p}B_c -> B_c, plus its inverse log_{c_p}, plus the Einstein midpoint (hyperbolic barycentre) and the curvature-implied sphere-area doubling radius sqrt-c * s with sinh(sqrt-c * s) = 2^{1/(n-1)} * sinh(sqrt-c * rho); curvature c = 1 fixed.
ideas.key_change: Every 250 Stage 2 epochs, for each level-l prefix whose training-only successor distribution is significantly more than binary, insert ONE new level-(l+1) codeword at exp_{c_{l,k}}( s(rho) * u ), where u points from the parent codeword toward the Einstein barycentre of that prefix's empirical successors and s(rho) is the curvature-implied doubling radius around the parent's own item cloud.
ideas.leakage_boundary: C is built only from training-split sequences; no validation or test interaction, no test item, no test session is ever read during SID construction. SID refresh passes use only training-item assignments from Stage 2 forward passes on training batches. The Stage 3 generator sees only the final exported codebooks and SID table; nothing in the growth operator conditions on Stage 3 data, and the validation set is used only for the frozen protocol's logging/none of the mechanism.
ideas.motivation: In an RQ-VAE SID hierarchy the code capacity per level is fixed a priori and shared by every prefix, so prefixes whose users actually branch into several successor interests are forced to share a codeword with unrelated items while quiet prefixes hoard unused codewords. The result is SID prefixes whose next-token distribution is behaviourally ambiguous, which is exactly what the Stage 3 generative recommender must then model. Fixed capacity is the problem; the shape of the latent (curved) is the resource that should be spent where behaviour branches.
ideas.novelty: Previous rounds touched the assignment rule (radial/cone/weighted), the codebook averaging rule (Frechet, successor-weighted), the per-level curvature value (CURVCTRL), the successor profile smoothing and the codebook target shift. None of them changed the CARDINALITY/TOPOLOGY of the hierarchy. Here nothing about the assignment score and nothing about the codebook update rule changes: the mechanism is a growth operator that inserts codewords at behaviourally branching prefixes, with the insertion point and its spacing produced by the Poincare exp map at the parent codeword and a curvature-derived doubling radius. Behaviour supplies the WHICH (successor entropy) and the DIRECTION (successor Einstein barycentre); geometry supplies the POSITION and the SPACING. Removing either leaves a different operator, so the coupling is in the operator itself, not in a loss term beside it.
ideas.observables: (a) SID assignment: number of codewords per level and the fraction of items whose level-(l+1) index changes after a growth pass; (b) prefix behaviour predictability: mean successor entropy H(p) over level-l prefixes before/after, and the parent-prefix purity of the new codewords' item mass; (c) parameter update: the new codewords' gradients and usage counts in the epochs after insertion; (d) Stage 3 test_recall@10 against the 0.065 target.
risks: Growth may be too slow to matter (12 passes, entropy threshold rarely exceeded after the first passes); new codewords may be dead on arrival if the encoder's residual distribution is concentrated away from the parent ball; level-(l+1) codes shared across prefixes could let unrelated items steal a new codeword, blurring the prefix; curvature-derived radius could exceed the useful residual scale and be clipped constantly; Stage 2 codebook non-stationarity may destabilise the commitment loss in late epochs; single-run seed noise may swamp a real but small gain.
ideas.safeguards:
all distances clamp arcosh argument to >= 1+1e-8; Poincare norms clamped to 1/(1+1e-5) after every exp map; rho_p and s_p clipped to [1e-3, 0.5*R_max] with R_max the 99.9th percentile of the epoch's residual distances (measured, scale-relative, not tuned); duplicate-codeword rejection at 1e-3 curvature distance; entropy computed with pi floor 1e-12 and renormalised; prefixes with |S_p| < 2, zero outgoing mass or

a single dominant successor (pi_max > 1 - 1/|C_l|) are never split; new codewords protected from usage-based retirement for one pass; growth is idempotent-safe if a pass finds nothing to split; the whole operator is skipped if C is empty (behaviour-off switch); no gradient flows through the growth operator (detached embeddings), so Stage 2's loss is untouched.
ideas.spec_equations: pass at epoch e in E: for l = 1..L-1: for each prefix p at level l with |S_p| >= 2 and Z_p > 0: pi_p(j) = mass(S_p -> S_j)/Z_p; H_p = -sum_j pi_p(j) log pi_p(j); support_ok = (at least two j have pi_p(j) >= 1/|C_l|); if H_p > log 2 and support_ok: rho_p = clip(median_{i in S_p} d_c(v_i, c_{l,k}), 1e-3, 0.5*R_max); u_p = log_{c_{l,k}}(b_p)/max(||log_{c_{l,k}}(b_p)||_L, 1e-8); s_p = arcsinh( 2^{1/(n-1)} * sinh(rho_p) ); s_p = min(s_p, 0.5*R_max); cand = exp_{c_{l,k}}( s_p * u_p ); if ||cand||_P >= 1/(1+1e-5): cand = cand*( (1/(1+1e-5)) / ||cand||_P ); threshold check: if d_c(cand, any existing C_{l+1}[k]) > 1e-3: append cand to C_{l+1}, reset its optimizer state, mark it protected for one pass from usage death; then recompute the SID table for all 24556 training items with the curved RQ assignment rule and continue training. Per-pass insertion cap: at most |C_l| per level (<= doubling), which the entropy gate never realistically reaches.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: frozen sparse training transition matrix C (24556 x 24556, ~2e6 nnz cap), item embeddings v_i of the training items in B_c^n, current codebooks C_1..C_L, current item->prefix assignment. Outputs: grown codebooks C_1..C_L, an updated SID table (24556 x L), and a per-pass log (prefix p, H_p, rho_p, s_p, parent index, new index) for the diagnostics.

specification.text: Lorentz/Poincare ball B_c^n, curvature -c, c=1 fixed (documented default, NOT trained, NOT swept). Standard curved RQ: v = encoder(item) in B_c^n; r_0 = v; level l: k_l = argmin_k d_c(r_{l-1}, C_l[k]), r_l = exp_0( log_{C_l[k_l]}( r_{l-1} ) ). SID = (k_1..k_L). Growth operator G (see SPEC EQUATIONS) runs at epochs E = {250,500,...,3000} (12 passes); it reads only cached training transition counts C and cached item assignments, appends codewords to C_2..C_L, refreshes the SID table, and never touches Stage 3. Growth threshold log(2) nats and mass floor 1/|C_l| are derived, not tuned; curvature c=1 and doubling factor 2 (one split -> two children) are documented defaults.

ideas.title: Behaviour-gestated hyperbolic codebook growth: successor-entropy decides which SID prefix splits, negative curvature decides where the new codeword is born.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: m_i := 0 for all i, so every basepoint is the origin and the chain reduces to the origin-chart curved RQ (curvature, distance and maps unchanged, successor table computed but unused). Code path: BEHAV=off short-circuits basepoint construction before the centroid lookup.
ideas.ablation_both_on: BEHAV=on and GEOM=poincare, i.e. successor Lorentzian centroid -> exp_0(lambda_l log_0 .) basepoint -> log_b / exp_b quantizer. This is the only arm trained in the round.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: the same successor centroids and level schedule are used, but m_i is a weighted Euclidean mean, exp/log are the identity, Moebius addition is +, and d_P is the Euclidean distance: the chain becomes a behaviour-anchored Euclidean residual quantizer. Code path: GEOM=euclid dispatches to flat_ops.
ideas.behavior_computation: One pass over training sessions only: for every consecutive pair (i_t, i_{t+1}) with i_t != i_{t+1}, increment N[i_t, i_{t+1}] by 1 (user-id-level dedup so a user counts once per pair). Normalise p(j|i) = N[i,j] / sum_j N[i,j], truncate to the top-K = 20 successors, and treat items with no outgoing transitions as having m_i = 0 (origin). The centroid uses an item-representation buffer e_i that is an EMA (0.9) of the tanh-mapped encoder outputs produced for training items, always detached, so no gradient flows through the behaviour side.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed next-item transitions within sessions (sequential co-consumption), restricted to the Stage 2 training split, giving per item a successor distribution p(j|i).
ideas.cost_estimate: Transition table built once from the Stage 2 training split: sparse counts over 24556 items, truncated to 24556 x 20 = 491k entries, O(nnz) memory (~4 MB at fp32 with indices), built in seconds. The basepoint table m_i (24556 x d) is recomputed once per epoch: 24556 x 20 lifts + weighted Minkowski sums + projections, about 16 MFLOP at d = 64, i.e. under 0.1 s per epoch, 3000 epochs = about 5 minutes total. Per step (24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps) the extra work is a table lookup plus B x K lifts and one centroid projection for the batch, about B*K*d = 1024*20*64 = 1.3 MFLOP, plus 2L exp/log maps per item (6 maps at B = 1024 -> 6144 artanh/tanh) - well under 2% of the encoder+decoder step, so wall clock is roughly +2 to +4% over the frozen Stage 2 budget with no extra epochs.
ideas.coupling_equation: b_i^(l) = exp_0( lambda_l * log_0( m_i ) ),  m_i = LorentzCentroid( { e_j : j in TopK(p(.|i)) }, p(j|i) ),  k_l = argmin_k d_P( exp_{ b_i^(l) }( t_l ), C_k ),  t_{l+1} = t_l - log_{ b_i^(l) }( C_{k_l} ).
ideas.coupling_path:
behaviour -> basepoint -> chart -> assignment -> residual -> reconstruction loss -> encoder and codebook gradient. The behaviour distribution produces the centroid m_i; the centroid is transported by exp_0 into the ball to become the chart basepoint b_i^(l); b_i^(l) is the origin of the log map that produces the level-1 tangent vector, so the same vector z_i is compared with a different codebook entry (and produces a different residual) than under the origin chart, and the gradient of the reconstruction loss flows through log_{b} and hence through m_i. Setting BEHAV=off collapses b to 0 and the whole chain becom

es the flat origin-chart RQ; setting GEOM=euclid replaces Moebius/exp/log/d_P by Euclidean mean, identity maps and L2 distance while keeping the same basepoint table, so removing either one demonstrably changes the assignment, the residual and the gradient.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis:
If the first digit is allowed to encode the behavioural future rather than the item identity, then (i) SIDs of items with sharp successor distributions move toward their dominant successor in the ball while diffuse items stay near the origin, (ii) prefix-conditioned successor predictability computed on training transitions from the top-1 prefix rises relative to the origin

-chart baseline, and (iii) Stage 3 test recall@10 exceeds 0.065 in the single frozen run. It would be observed as higher train-only adjacency/coherence diagnostics for high-branching items and as the recall number itself; both are recorded, recall judges.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the residual quantizer, at every level l of the RQ chain: the chart basepoint exp_0(lambda_l log_0 m_i) defines where the level is quantized and decoded, and the reconstruction/commitment distances d_P are measured there. It also propagates back through the encoder gradient (the log/exp maps are differentiable), so the parameter update is curved.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball of fixed negative curvature c = 1 (metric factor lambda_x = 2/(1-||x||^2)); explicit curved operations: Moebius addition, exponential map exp_x, logarithmic map log_x, Poincare distance d_P, and the Lorentzian (hyperboloid) weighted centroid used as the barycentre (a closed-form Frechet mean), all at c = 1.
ideas.key_change: Replace z -> q1 -> r1 -> q2 -> ... with t1 = log_{b_i^(1)}(z_i), k_l = argmin_k d_P(exp_{b_i^(l)}(t_l), C_k), t_{l+1} = t_l - log_{b_i^(l)}(C_{k_l}), where b_i^(l) = exp_0(lambda_l * log_0(m_i)) and m_i is the Lorentzian centroid of the EMA embeddings of i's top-K training successors. Decoding is z_hat = exp_{b_i^(L)}(sum_l log_{b_i^(l)}(C_{k_l})), and the reconstruction distance is measured in the same chart.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition counts, the top-K successor lists, the EMA buffer and every basepoint are computed exclusively from Stage 2 training-split sessions (plus representations of training items produced by the model itself). Validation and test interactions are never read: the tables are frozen before Stage 3, the Stage 3 prefix-tree/beam protocol consumes only the learned codebooks and the chart of the *context* item built from training transitions, and no validation- or test-derived statistic enters the SID assignment, the basepoints or the codebooks.
ideas.motivation: In a flat multi-level RQ-VAE every item lives in one shared chart anchored at the origin, so the coarse digit must describe both what the item is and what it leads to, and the encoder has no way to spend its first prefix on the behavioural future. Items with many, diffuse or strongly skewed next-item distributions get the same geometry as leaf-like items, so their prefixes carry no transition information and Stage 3 generation drifts to globally popular but behaviourally wrong successors.
ideas.novelty: Earlier rounds changed the codebook (successor-weighted Frechet centre updates), the curvature per level (prefix-transition-driven curvature), or the radial gain of the assignment. Here the codebook, the curvature and the radius are untouched: what changes is the COORDINATE CHART (tangent-space basepoint) in which the residual chain is quantized and decoded, and the chart moves along the geodesic toward the item's successors as the level deepens. The behaviour signal therefore changes the metric origin of every digit, not the dictionary and not the distance.
ideas.observables: SID digit l of an item changes (assignment flips) as a monotone function of its successor concentration (1 - normalised entropy of p(.|i)) and of its radius; the fraction of items whose digit-1 code is shared with at least one of their training successors increases; train-only prefix-to-successor predictability rises; Stage 3 test recall@10 is the single judged number and must exceed 0.065.
risks: The EMA buffer lags early in training so m_i is initially a stale centroid (mitigated by initialising the buffer from the first forward pass and detaching it); the level schedule can push basepoints so far out that the coarse prefix becomes item-specific and prefix reuse collapses; the tangent-space residual subtraction is exact only in the small-residual regime, so large-radius items can accumulate reconstruction error; low-count transitions can produce noisy centroids; the chart change could simply be absorbed by the encoder and leave Stage 3 unchanged.
ideas.safeguards: clamp ||m_i|| to 1 - 1e-3 and z to r_max = 1 - 1e-3 before any log/artanh; clip the artanh argument to 1 - 1e-6; return 0 for log_x(x) and use a 1e-8 norm floor on every v/||v||; detach the EMA buffer and the successor table from the graph (no gradient through behaviour counts); fall back to b = 0 for items with zero outgoing transitions or empty buffers; renormalise the Lorentz centroid if -<y,y>_M <= 1e-8; keep codebook entries inside the ball by the same clamp after each EMA update; guard against NaN by skipping the EMA write for a code whose assigned count is 0 in the step; raise the level schedule only after the first epoch so the buffer is warm; deterministic top-K tie-breaking by item index so the chart is reproducible.
ideas.spec_equations:
Poincare ball D = {x in R^d : ||x|| < 1}, c = 1, lambda_x = 2/(1-||x||^2).
Moebius: x (+) y = [ (1 + 2<x,y> + ||y||^2) x + (1 - ||x||^2) y ] / (1 + 2<x,y> + ||x||^2 ||y||^2).
exp_x(v) = x (+) ( tanh(||v||/2) * v / ||v|| ) for v != 0, else x.
log_x(y) = 2 * artanh(||(-x) (+) y||) * ((-x) (+) y) / ||(-x) (+) y||, 0 if y = x.
d_P(x,y) = 2 * artanh( ||(-x) (+) y|| ).
Lift: xi(x) = ( (1+||x||^2)/(1-||x||^2), 2x/(1-||x||^2) ) in R^{d+1}, Minkowski form <a,b>_M = -a0 b0 + sum_{i>=1} a_i b_i.
LorentzCentroid({x_j}, w_j): y = sum_j w_j xi(x_j) (sum_j w_j = 1); y <- y / sqrt(-<y,y>_M); return y_{1:} / (y_0 + 1).
Basepoint: u_i = log_0(m_i) = 2 artanh(||m_i||) m_i/||m_i|| (0 if m_i = 0); b_i^(l) = exp_0(lambda_l u_i), lambda_l = 1 - 2^(-l), l = 1..L.
Encoder output z_i = r_max * tanh(W h_i) with r_max = 1 - 1e-3, so z_i is inside the ball by construction.
Quantizer (per item i, levels l = 1..L, L = 3):
  t_1 = log_{b_i^(1)}(z_i)
  for l = 1..L:  k_l = argmin_k d_P( exp_{b_i^(l)}(t_l), C_l[k] )
                 a_l = log_{b_i^(l)}( C_l[k_l] )
                 t_{l+1} = t_l - a_l
  z_hat = exp_{b_i^(L)}( sum_{l=1..L} a_l )
Loss: L_rec = d_P(z_hat, z_i)^2 ; L_commit = d_P(z_i, exp_{b_i^(1)}( stopgrad(t_1) ))^2 + sum_l d_P( stopgrad(exp_{b_i^(l)}(t_l)), exp_{b_i^(l)}(a_l) )^2 weighted as in the baseline beta; codebooks updated by the baseline EMA rule in ball coordinates on the assigned (exp_{b}(t_l)) points.
Successor table: N[i,j] from training sessions; p(j|i) = N[i,j]/sum_j N[i,j]; TopK 20.
Buffers: e_i <- 0.9 e_i + 0.1 tanh(W h_i).detach(), initialised on the first epoch's forward passes.
Pseudocode:
  build_transitions(train_sessions) -> (idx, p)
  each epoch: m = LorentzCentroidTable(e, idx, p, K) ; b[l] = exp0(lambda_l * log0(m))
  each step: z = r_max*tanh(enc(x)); b_i

= b[l][batch]; run charted residual chain above; loss; backward; EMA codebook; EMA buffer.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: encoder latent z_i in the open unit ball (d dims), the frozen training successor table (indices + probabilities, K = 20), the EMA item buffer e (24556 x d), the level codebooks C_l (Kc x d in the ball), depth L and the fixed lambda_l schedule. Outputs: the discrete SID tuple (k_1,...,k_L), the reconstructed z_hat in the ball, the reconstruction/commitment losses, and gradients w.r.t. encoder parameters and C_l. At inference the same basepoint is built for the *context* item from training transitions only, and beam search over (k_1..k_L) uses the same chart.

specification.text: See SPEC EQUATIONS. Constants are fixed, not tuned: curvature c = 1 (unit Poincare ball, documented default), depth schedule lambda_l = 1 - 2^(-l) for l = 1..L (forces the chart to open at the midpoint toward the future and to converge to it), K = 20 successors (documented default, truncated by training transition count), EMA momentum 0.9 (documented default). Switches BEHAV in {on, off} and GEOM in {poincare, euclid} exist in the code; the single run uses BEHAV=on, GEOM=poincare.

ideas.title: Successor-barycentre tangent charts: the RQ-VAE residual chain is quantized in a per-item Poincare tangent chart whose basepoint is the hyperbolic centroid of the item's training-only successor distribution, and that basepoint slides toward the behavioural future level by level.

objective: Improve the semantic IDs of a generative recommender: a training-only behaviour signal must guide the whole SID prefix hierarchy in a hyperbolic RQ-VAE, and the result must raise the Stage 3 test recall above 0.065.
